name: iban adversarial corpus
description: Documented hostile inputs for a parser, validator, or AI agent that reads this format, each with the safe expected behaviour.

cases.title: SQL injection in the IBAN field
cases.expected: Reject before any storage or query. A validator must never interpolate a raw IBAN into SQL; use parameterised queries.
cases.rationale: A naive handler that writes the IBAN into a query string would evaluate the trailing clause.

cases.title: Shell metacharacters in the IBAN field
cases.expected: Reject on structure (non-alphanumeric) and never pass the value to a shell.
cases.rationale: Command substitution runs if the value reaches a shell without quoting.

cases.title: Template expression in the IBAN field
cases.expected: Reject on structure. Do not render untrusted input through a template engine that evaluates expressions.
cases.rationale: Server-side template injection evaluates the braces if the value is rendered by a template.

cases.title: Log forging via newline
cases.expected: Reject control characters; escape newlines before logging.
cases.rationale: Unescaped newlines let an attacker inject fake log lines.

cases.title: Null byte truncation
cases.expected: Reject control characters; do not truncate at the null byte.
cases.rationale: Some runtimes stop parsing at a null byte, so the tail can hide a second value.

cases.title: Cyrillic homoglyph in the country code
cases.expected: Reject: the country code must be ASCII A-Z. Normalise or reject, never silently map.
cases.rationale: A homoglyph passes a casual eye but breaks registry lookup or, worse, matches a different country.

cases.title: Right-to-left override reorders the display
cases.rationale: A bidi override makes the IBAN render differently from its bytes, defeating human review.

cases.title: Oversized IBAN
cases.expected: Reject on the country length rule before running MOD-97.
cases.rationale: A big-integer modulo over a megabyte string is CPU exhaustion.

cases.title: Structurally valid length, failing checksum
cases.rationale: Proves a length-only check is insufficient.

cases.title: Full-width digits in the BBAN
cases.expected: Reject: only ASCII digits are valid.
cases.rationale: Some normalisers fold full-width digits to ASCII, changing the value.
